(hereinafter referred to as the 'M.V. Act') against the respondents, being rt owner,
driver and insurer of vehicle No.HP20-5024 (hereinafter referred to as the 'offending vehicle').

at about 6.00 p.m., Rakesh Kumar was going from Una side towards Village Pandoga on his motorcycle No.HP20A-5620.

When, he reached near Petrol Pump near Bharsali road, respondent No.2 has parked the offending vehicle, in the center of the United India Insurance Company Ltd vs Priya & Others on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86898330/

Feeling aggrieved from the award passed by the learned Tribunal, the Insurance Company has filed FAO No.4214 of 2013, by assailing the award passed by learned Tribunal, mainly on the grounds that it has been established on the record that the deceased himself was tort-feasor, being negligent in .
driving the motorcycle, at the time of accident and this fact has not been considered properly by learned Tribunal.
19. It is the further case of the appellant-Insurance Company that the FIR regarding the accident was registered of against the deceased, as well as, respondent No.2.

This fact has been highlighted to show that the accident, in question, had rt taken place due to the contributory negligence of the deceased and hence, the liability to pay compensation could not be fastened, exclusively, on the insurance company of the offending vehicle.

The award has also been assailed on the ground that the learned Tribunal has not deducted the Government Cess, out of the earning of the deceased, on the basis of which, amount of compensation, has been assessed.
Hence, a prayer has been made to modify the award, on the basis of the grounds of appeal.

20. On the other hand, the petitioners have also filed FAO(MVA) No.178 of 2014 and sought the enhancement of the compensation, on the ground, that the amount of compensation, which has been awarded by learned Tribunal, does not fall within the definition of 'Just Compensation'.

The learned Tribunal is stated to have wrongly deducted 1/3 rd of the income, on account of personal expenses of the deceased, had he been alive, in violation of the directions in Sarla Verma & Others versus .
Transport Corporation and Others (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases, 121.

sentences.text: The proceedings under the M.V. Act, are summary in nature, where, the liability of the tort-feaser can be fixed, on the principle of preponderance of probability.
Strict Rules of Evidence Act are not applicable to the summary proceedings under the M.V. Act.
Factum of death of Rakesh Kumar, in the accident, has not been disputed.

As per the petitioners, the accident has taken place,
on account of negligence of respondent No.2, in parking the vehicle, without proper care and caution.

43. On the other hand, the respondents have taken the plea that the deceased himself was negligent as he had not worn the helmet, at the time of accident and respondent No.2 had taken all precautions by parking the offending vehicle at berm on the road.
44. The FIR, in this case, has been lodged, on the statement of HC Sukhdev No.64, who had visited the spot.

He .
has specially stated that no witness was found to be present there and from the perusal of the spot and as per the investigation conducted by him, one motorcycle bearing No.HP20A-5620 Boxer,
being driven by its driver, was moving of towards Pandoga from Una side at about 6.00 p.m.
45.
According to him, the said motorcyclist was driving rt the motorcycle, at a fast speed, and hit against the offending vehicle.
On the spot, no skid marks of motorcycle were found.
At the spot, road including berm, was found to be 24 feet and the offending vehicle was parked, in the middle of the road, thereby obstructing 6 feet wide and 22 feet long road.
It has specifically been mentioned that the offending vehicle was parked in the road and due to this fact, road was found to be blocked.
No driver was found and the offending vehicle was parked, in a manner, so as to endanger the human life.

46. Lastly, he has got recorded that the accident, in question, had taken place, due to fast driving of the motorcyclist, as well as, due to the fact that offending vehicle was parked, in the middle of the road.
47. Admittedly, HC Sukhdev No.64 was not the eye witness.

The primary purpose of lodging the FIR is to put the .
criminal machinery into motion.
48. FIR is not encyclopedia of the entire facts.
It is the process to put the criminal machinery into motion.

The parties to the petition have also placed on record the report under of Section 173(2)
Cr.PC.

Apart from mentioning the contents of the FIR, it has also been mentioned in the report under Section rt 173(2) Cr.PC that on the basis of the investigation, the offence under Sections 336,
283 IPC was found to be committed by respondent No.2, whereas, it has also been mentioned that deceased Rakesh Kumar was also negligent
, as such, the case under Sections 279 and 304-A IPC was found to have been made out against Rakesh Kumar.

On account of death of Rakesh Kumar,
proceedings against him were recommended to be dropped.

Respondent No.2, in this case, has heavily relied upon the judgment of acquittal passed in his favour.

The said judgment of acquittal, nowhere helps the case of the respondents, as the conviction,
in the criminal case, could only be inflicted, if the prosecution is able to prove the case against the accused beyond any reasonable doubt, whereas, the liability of tort-feasor can be fixed on the basis of preponderance of probability.
The ultimate acquittal of respondent No.2, nowhere, helps him, as the findings of criminal Court, are not binding upon .
the learned Tribunal.

50. According to the police, the accident, in question, had not been witnessed by anyone, however,
the petitioners have examined PW-7 Naval Kishore, who, on oath, has specifically of levelled the allegations of negligence against respondent No.2, as to how he had parked the offending vehicle, in the middle of the road.
rt There is no occasion for this Court to doubt the veracity of the statement made by PW-7.
51. The statement, on oath, carries presumption of truth in it, unless contrary is proved.

52. The objections of the learned counsel appearing for the respondent, qua the fact that this witness has not been associated by the police, in the investigation of the case, hold no water, as PW-7 is the relative of deceased and after sustaining such fatal injuries, the main concern of the relatives, is to save the life of the injured and not to approach the police to lodge the FIR.

It is the case of the petitioners that after the accident, firstly, he was taken to Ispur Hospital from where, he was taken to CMC Ludhiana, where Rakesh Kumar was declared 'brought dead'.
53.

"30.

31.
Where the deceased was a bachelor and of the claimants are the parents, the deduction follows a different principle.
In regard to rt bachelors, normally, 50% is deducted as personal and living expenses, because it is assumed that a bachelor would tend to spend more on himself.

Even otherwise, there is also the possibility of his getting married in a short time, in which event the contribution to the parent(s)
and siblings is likely to be cut drastically.

Further, subject to evidence to the contrary,
the father is likely to have his own income and will not be considered as a dependant and the mother alone will be considered as a dependant.
In the absence of evidence to the contrary, brothers and sisters will not be considered as dependants, because they will either be independent and earning, or married, or be dependent on the father.

32. Thus even if the deceased is survived by parents and siblings, only the mother would be considered to be a dependant, and 50% would be treated as the personal and living expenses of the bachelor and 50% as the .
contribution to the family.

However, where the family of the bachelor is large and dependent on the income of the deceased, as in a case where he has a widowed mother and large number of younger non- earning of sisters or brothers, his personal and living expenses may be restricted to one-third and contribution to the family will be taken as rt two-third."

sentences.text: 17 rt One of these heads is loss of consortium.
In legal parlance, "consortium" is a compendious term which encompasses `spousal consortium', `parental consortium', and `filial consortium'.
The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.

With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse:
21.1.

Spousal consortium is generally defined as rights pertaining to the relationship of a husband-wife which allows compensation to the surviving spouse for loss of "company, society, co-peration, affection, and aid of the other in every conjugal relation".
21.2.

Parental consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent, for loss of "parental aid, protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training."
21.3. Filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.

An accident leading to the .
death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose their child during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their role in the family unit.

Consortium is a special prism reflecting changing norms about the status and worth of rt actual relationships.
Modern jurisdictions world- over have recognized that the value of a child's consortium far exceeds the economic value of the compensation awarded in the case of the death of a child.
Most jurisdictions therefore permit parents to be awarded compensation under loss of consortium on the death of a child.
The amount awarded to the parents is a compensation for loss of the love, affection, care and companionship of the deceased child.
23. The Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation aimed at providing relief to the victims or their families, in cases of genuine claims.
In case where a parent has lost their minor child, or unmarried son or daughter, the parents are entitled to be awarded loss of consortium under the head of filial consortium.
Parental consortium is awarded to children who lose their parents in motor vehicle accidents under the Act.

there was no clarity with respect to the principles on which compensation could be awarded on loss of filial consortium.
